frequency_question: How often does the central bank use a temporary incremental reserve ratio when systemic liquidity is heavily skewed by structural inflows?
membership_rule: Includes any formal regulatory mandate forcing banks to hold a higher marginal reserve ratio on incremental liabilities above a specific baseline date. Excludes standard statutory liquidity ratio changes or permanent cash reserve ratio hikes.
provenance_note: 2 cases named, 3 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.5x)
coverage_note: 2 named instances of iCRR specifically deployed by the RBI in modern history; 1 prior non-iCRR absorption cycle using alternative market stabilization schemes.
known_gaps: Limited to modern central banking frameworks where secondary sterilization bonds were supplemented by direct marginal ratio freezes.
skeleton: RBI liquidity management interventions categorized by systemic shocks requiring non-standard marginal absorption over three distinct multi-year tightening phases.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 3 major liquidity overhang cycles equals 67 percent base rate.
validity_reason: Central bank institutional toolkits for liquidity management evolve slowly over multi-year monetary policy regimes.
